review_text: Close your eyes and image the perfect face mask. An at-home spa treatment, with a smooth cream-like texture, the perfect face mask is at once rich yet gentle, and kind to sensitive skin. It soothes and hydrates tired skin, its anti-inflammatory qualities helping to clear blemishes (see you never pesky pimple!). Just having it on your face feels amazing, as the perfect face masks calms the skin, giving it a slight tingle and cooling sensation. I actually love this stuff because the salicylic acid content seems to be high enough to dry pimples and keep pimple-prone areas free of acne without over-drying. (I do wish they listed what the percentage of salicylic acid is.)  ...Anyway, I’ve been using this for quite awhile, and the key to making it work is to NOT shake it up and to thoroughly and deeply dip your swab down into the powder, really getting the swab fully covered thickly in the salicylic powder, and then dab it on your zits, and even lightly dab on acne-prone areas. This has helped me immensely to both get rid of pimples and to keep acne-prone areas pimple-free. You really need to get a lot of that white salicylic powder on your swab so that you can put a thick-ish layer of it on pimples, otherwise it will be too diluted to work optimally.

review_text: HOW this oil gives my skin a matte look I will never know but it DOES! I am a huge fan of The Ordinary’s rose hip seed oil but this chia seed oil is everything I imagined it would be and more. I’m used to adding chia seeds in my yogurt or oatmeal and the seeds suck the moisture out of my food and plump up to twice their size. So, I had a feeling this would probably pull the oil out of my skin and plump up my skin. Well, I didn’t notice any plumping effects but I definitely noticed my oiliness disappeared. Typically, when I use oils as moisturizers, they take time to sink into my skin and they leave my skin greasy to the touch. This oil left my skin instantly so smooth and soft. I add three drops to my hand and rub them together before applying and it feels like I have more of a water based liquid in my hand than an oil. This is definitely more of a dry oil but it is very moisturizing and I don’t have that tight skin feel nor any dryness on my skin when I apply this after cleansing. I am so in love with this oil! I still love the rose hip seed oil for it’s healing effects but I will definitely be using this chia seed oil during the day to help combat any oiliness.

I have very sensitive, combination skin, and the toner and moisturizer has caused me to have cystic acne on my forehead. I did a few elimination experiments to see if everything in the kit was the culprit and this is what I found:The Cleanser: Is awesome! I really enjoy it. I use it as often as I shower, after I’ve removed my makeup, but not daily. I don’t recommend using any type of acid treatments or AHA/BHA treatments after using it- save those for other days of the week with calmer cleansers. The Toner: Is the culprit. I tried it a few times over a span of months and each time I had the same result.The Moisturizer: Is not for sensitive skin. review_text: I received the Microderm Elite complimentary from PMD Beauty for testing purposes. A little bit about my skin before diving into this review - I have sensitive, oily, acne-prone skin. I was honestly impressed at the overall experience of the kit - I liked having multiple caps and discs to choose from depending on the type of treatment I wanted to do - face, body, or even blackhead focused. However, I was most impressed by the thorough instructions the brand provides in the booklet that comes with the device. PMD explains the different components in the kit and provides instructions on how to use the device - which is essential for this type of tool. As someone with sensitive skin, I use the lowest setting and most gentle disc. My skin felt a little sore immediately after my first treatment, but I’m not surprised given my sensitive skin as well as the nature of the device and the fact that I am still getting used to using the tool. Don’t apply pressure to the device and make sure to keep it moving as you use it. Never go over the same area multiple times in one treatment! I personally have yet to see noticeable changes to my skin - but with regular use, I expect to see an impact. The *sole* reason I am giving this tool a 4-star rating is due to the complexity/learning curve when you first use the device. When I first tried the device on my arm, the suction was stronger than I expected, so the device got stuck in one spot and left a red mark. Be sure to read the instructions, watch the online tutorial on the website, and test on the arm prior to using on the face! With all the above said, I’d recommend the device to experienced skincare lovers looking for this type of at-home treatment.

review_text: I’m really loving these. I worked for a dermatologist for 10 years and am very familiar with dermaplaning practices. I’d say this is a great product for beginners, especially if a spa/derm isn’t in your budget or of any interest. The most important thing is the angle at which you hold the razor and not performing this too frequently (over-exfoliation is a def a thing). Make sure you’re always holding the razor at a 45-degree angle against your skin. Short downward strokes are the best way to go when you’re dermaplaning at home after you cleanse and dry your face. Keeping the skin taut and moving from top to bottom is the general rule of thumb. Take it slow too and be conscious of the unique angles/curves of your face. Dermaplaning is a very intuitive practice! I’d recommend only doing it every 3 to 4 weeks for optimal results. Afterward, avoid direct sun exposure/extreme heat for a few days days, don’t use scrubs or other exfoliators for a week, avoid chlorine on your face for a week, apply serums, moisturizers, and sunscreen as usual.

review_text: I purchased this product from the Glossier website as a set with a 1oz bottle of Futuredew (pro tip: Glossier’s products are a fair amount cheaper if you purchase them as sets, so I would find products you like and match them with a set that contains all/most of them!). The bottle of cleanser itself is fairly large, with a pump that dispenses a nice amount. I used to start off my day with two pumps of Glossier’s Milky Jelly Cleanser. It is very gentle and smooth, but I’m still not too sure how effective it really is. It is really good at removing obvious makeup/dirt/impurities from the previous night if there’s any remaining, but you don’t get that “squeaky clean“ feeling that you would get from a product like the Kiehl’s cleanser. That said, it is kind of nice that this product feels almost moisturizing, as opposed to drying, since some cleansers feel that way on the skin! It has a very subtle but nice rose scent, so it’s technically not fragrance-free, but I read in the ingredients that the fragrance is “under 1% and formulated without Acetaldehyde, Acetone, Acetonitrile, Benzalkonium chloride, BPA, EDTA, Methylene chloride, PTFE, PFOA“, so it shouldn’t be overwhelming to most people. Additionally, I have to give props to how this product is Clean at Sephora, cruelty-free, vegan, and formulated without sulfates SLS and SLES - I’m very glad how Sephora has made an effort to bring in more clean beauty products/brands - especially such a mainstream one like Glossier!All in all, a 6oz bottle of this cleanser lasted me just under a year, which is really good considering I used two pumps of this 1-2 times a day. It’s not the cheapest cleanser at $19, but I would say if you’re looking for a gentle cleanser that feels soft on the skin, I would splurge on this. However, if you’re looking for a sudsy, more “squeaky clean“ feeling cleanser that strips skin of everything (potentially including a bit of moisture, if you’re okay with that), I’d go with something else.
